summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 20.5% YoY to INR932 crore with normalized EBITDA margin of 19.31%, aided by 7-8% price hikes.
summary.overview: Management reported its best-ever Q2, with total revenue up 20.5% YoY to INR932 crore and normalized EBITDA up 30.2% to INR180 crore (margin 19.31%, +143 bps). PAT was INR164.3 crore, lifted by a INR50 crore exceptional gain from a slump sale to ACE KATO Private Limited. Pricing actions of 7-8% were implemented by end-September, with only about 3% realised in H1; further steel-driven price hikes are planned for late Q3 or early Q4, likely shifting to January. Management guided 18-20% revenue growth for FY27 and sustained EBITDA margins.

financial_highlights.metric: Exceptional gain (slump sale to ACE KATO)
Cranes, material handling & construction equipment revenue (Q2)
financial_highlights.value: INR788 crore (89% of revenue); segment EBITDA margin 18.65%; segment EBITDA INR147 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Investments plus cash and bank balance (Sept 2026)

segments.name: Cranes, material handling & construction equipment
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR788 crore (+13.54% YoY), EBITDA INR147 crore at 18.65% margin (+50 bps). Units sold 2,812 (+20% YoY). Realisations fell YoY on mix, per management.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR47.49 crore (about 6% of total). H1 realisation up about 23% YoY, attributed to product mix and an export order; management said agri demand domestically has moderated and passing on prices is getting difficult.

segments.name: Others (mainly exports and parts)
segments.commentary: Management said this line typically runs INR60-70 crore a year; Q2 reported figure of about INR48 crore was mostly export orders (about INR40-45 crore), with some Q1 shipments stuck in logistics.

segments.name: Defence
segments.commentary: Rough terrain cranes, telehandlers and heavy recovery cranes began delivery in Q1. Defence order book about INR500 crore over 1.5-2 years; a 74-unit backhoe loader order for BRO to be delivered in Q4 (about INR20-25 crore).

segments.name: ACE KATO JV
segments.commentary: Operations commenced in the previous quarter. Medium-term revenue target INR300-400 crore over 2.5-3 years; FY28 at least INR150 crore; target EBITDA about 15% at operating level (10-12% initially).

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20%, with possibly more if volumes scale.
EBITDA margins expected to be sustained through cost efficiency, mix and operating leverage.
Further calibrated price increases expected late Q3 or early Q4 (likely January) after steel rose about 10-12% in October; management said it will try to avoid margin impact.
Expected operating leverage of 2-3% of margin once revenue reaches INR5,000-5,500 crore in one to two years; part may be passed to customers.

Export-specific JV models expected FY29-FY30, with INR200-500 crore export potential cited; new products (aerial work platforms, reach stackers, piling rigs) each seen at INR150-200 crore in 2-3 years.
Inventory expected to normalise to INR500-600 crore by December-end or March; short-term borrowings to normalise by December or March.
capex_capacity: Current utilisation about 55% in cranes and construction equipment at end-Q2 (now 70-75%); agri about 25-30%. Current capacity supports INR5,500-6,000 crore revenue.
New plant in existing premises for defence machines and new products: INR40-50 crore, expected commissioning January-February 2027.
Robotics, automation and continuous improvement capex INR30-40 crore; maintenance capex about INR20 crore.
Possible land purchase of about INR130 crore this year (registry and payments pending), with another INR130 crore plus or minus.
Tower crane capacity expansion of at least INR400 crore (land of about INR50 crore already procured); decision by end-November or December, with start in Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28.
demand_pricing: Price realisations up 7-8% across cranes, construction equipment and material handling by end-September; about 3% realised in H1 on a blended basis, with the balance from October.
Steel prices rose from INR48-50/kg to INR63-64/kg earlier, cooled below INR60, then rose to INR66-67/kg in October; input costs up above 10-12%, with about 8% passed on so far.
Order book at start of November described as healthy; management expects 55-60% of revenue in H2, with festive demand strong in September-October.
Backhoe loaders: about 150-160 machines per quarter last quarter vs about 190-200 in the latest quarter; Q3 expected to be stronger.
Rental segment accounts for about 50% of the market; management said pricing must stay viable for it.
Chinese excavator share has risen about 25% in five to six years; anti-dumping decision awaited in one to two months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cranes and MH realisations fall YoY despite pricing actions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited product mix (more forklifts, lower tonnage) and said it would analyse further. Blended H1 price gain was just over 3%, with 7-8% effective from late September/October.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses and impairment rise sharply QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said variable costs grew with revenue, and the rise in expected credit loss provisions is notional: 100% provision on government dues overdue beyond 180 days, not a cash loss.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ACE KATO JV outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Medium-term revenue INR300-400 crore in 2.5-3 years; FY28 at least INR150 crore; export models from FY29-30 could add INR200-500 crore. Targeted EBITDA about 15% (10-12% initially), with no anti-dumping or PLI benefit assumed.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and other current assets/liabilities rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Seasonal H2 build-up plus large defence orders (RTFLT and HRV) needing batch inspections; about INR100 crore linked to defence. GST paid on inventory is recoverable and will be set off against sales; advances of INR150-200 crore received.

qa_highlights.question: What is the treasury position and borrowing cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Average borrowing cost about 7%; surplus invested at about 3-4% alpha. About 70-80% of the portfolio is liquid, with 50% redeemable within a day. Short-term borrowings expected to normalise by December-March.

qa_highlights.question: What is the acquisition strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is working on and contemplating targets, with a preference for businesses of about INR400-500 crore revenue or slightly smaller, plus a possible larger deal; valuation and competitive advantage are key criteria.

risks_watch: Steel price volatility and a possible January price hike; customer pushback, particularly from repeat customers, and pressure on defence fixed-price orders.
Agri domestic demand moderating; realisation gains reliant on export orders.
Working capital: inventory of INR832 crore vs INR605 crore, GST blockage and short-term borrowings, to be normalised by Q4.
Anti-dumping decision on Chinese imports expected in one to two months; no ADD assumed in JV targets.
Tower crane capex timing (Q4 FY27 or Q1 FY28) and the tower crane decision due December.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and profitability, with explicit caution on steel-driven inflation. Management was evasive on the drivers of the YoY realisation dip and on the anti-dumping outcome. Answers on JV economics and capex timing were specific, but several figures were given as approximations.
key_quotes: Despite these external headwinds, the underlying fundamentals of the Indian economy remain strong.
We anticipate achieving 18%-20% revenue growth in FY27, supported by sustained operating performance.
Our first priority in the whole of this year, starting from April onwards, was to maintain profitability and sustain profitability, and we are very much focused on that.
We will never go overboard. That's one thing for sure.

adds.what: New plant in existing premises for defence machines and new products (INR40-50 crore)
Tower crane capacity expansion of at least INR400 crore (land ~INR50 crore already procured); decision pending end-Nov/Dec

growth.why: Management guided 18-20% FY27 revenue growth, backed by pricing of 7-8% (only ~3% realised in H1), a defence order book of ~INR500 crore, and a new INR40-50 crore plant due Jan-Feb 2027, with current capacity supporting INR5,500-6,000 crore revenue; the INR400 crore tower crane expansion is not yet approved and the INR130 crore land purchase is deferred, so the capacity backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided to sustaining EBITDA margins (Q2 normalized 19.31%, +143 bps YoY) via cost efficiency, mix and operating leverage, with 7-8% price hikes only ~3% realised in H1 and steel up 10-12% in October, so margin protection depends on pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Tower crane expansion of at least INR400 crore has land of about INR50 crore procured with decision due end-November or December; a INR40-50 crore defence/new-product plant is due to commission January-February 2027, but the tower crane project is not yet approved.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 18-20%, Q2 units sold up 20% YoY to 2,812, H2 expected at 55-60% of revenue, and a defence order book of about INR500 crore over 1.5-2 years, though utilisation of 55% (70-75% now) caps near-term volume.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation of about 55% in cranes and construction equipment (70-75% now) is not high enough to force capex, yet a tower crane expansion of at least INR400 crore decision is due end-November or December and a INR130 crore land purchase is pending.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said FY27 revenue growth of 18-20% could be exceeded if volumes scale, and Q2 revenue rose 20.5% YoY to INR932 crore, but the guide is only just set and H1 price gain was about 3%.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Steel rose to INR66-67/kg in October (input costs up 10-12%) with only about 8% passed on so far, fixed-price defence orders are exposed, and realisations fell YoY on mix despite 7-8% price hikes.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Defence rough terrain cranes, telehandlers and heavy recovery cranes began delivery in Q1; a 74-unit backhoe order is due Q4 (INR20-25 crore); aerial work platforms, reach stackers and piling rigs each seen at INR150-200 crore in 2-3 years.

rows.label: ACE KATO JV ramp-up and export JV models
rows.why: JV revenue target at least INR150 crore in FY28 and INR300-400 crore medium term over 2.5-3 years, with export JV potential of INR200-500 crore cited for FY29-FY30.

rows.label: Inventory and short-term borrowing normalisation
rows.why: Inventory at INR832 crore vs INR605 crore and GST blockage are expected to normalise to INR500-600 crore by December-end or March, with cash of about INR1,570 crore available.

rows.label: Second steel-linked price hike
rows.when: late Q3 to early Q4 FY27 (likely January)
rows.why: Steel rose about 10-12% in October with only about 8% of input inflation passed on so far, and management plans further calibrated price increases.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 18-20% FY27 growth guide and the ACE KATO JV, but cautious on steel-driven inflation and evasive on the drivers of the YoY realisation dip and the anti-dumping outcome.
